mainTopic: What counts as 'fire': roasting the פסח, ערלה fuel, coals, hot metal, and burning a בת כהן
overview: The עמוד opens with the last line of an earlier discussion: fresh vinegar keeps its sharpness, but used vinegar does not. The גמרא then explains why the משנה forbids roasting the פסח on a grill and yet tells a story of רבן גמליאל using one. A line is missing from the משנה: a grill with holes is allowed. רב אדא בר אהבה rules that bread baked in a swept oven that was heated with ערלה peels is permitted. He defends this ruling against רבי יוחנן's teaching that a swept oven is not 'צלי אש', and the גמרא gives two answers. Next comes רבי's ruling that a פסח placed on coals is צלי אש. This leads to a long discussion of what counts as 'fire': hot metal for צרעת, molten lead for the execution of a בת כהן, the גזירה שוה from בני אהרן, and רב נחמן's rule of מיתה יפה. Finally רבי ירמיה compares the פרים הנשרפים, and רבי זירא explains that the order of the words 'fire' and 'burning' makes the difference. The גמרא's pushback on that answer continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Fresh vinegar keeps its sharpness, used vinegar does not
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier answer: fresh vinegar still has its full sharpness, but vinegar that was already used has lost it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the sharpness of the fruit is still fully there. Here, the sharpness of the fruit is no longer fully there.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of an answer that started on the previous page. It explains why fresh vinegar works on meat but vinegar that was already used does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is not the kind of liquid but its strength. Fresh vinegar still has the fruit's sharpness, which can act on the meat and its blood. Once the vinegar has been used, that sharpness is spent, so the same rule no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: sharpness, the sour strength of vinegar
fruit (the fruit the vinegar came from)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the ending of a discussion from the previous עמוד, which is why it starts in the middle of a thought.

phrases.english: [there,] the sharpness of the fruit is intact.
phrases.notes: Describes fresh vinegar.

phrases.english: Here, there is not
phrases.notes: Describes vinegar that was already used.

phrases.english: the sharpness of the fruit in its intact state.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer from the previous page.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two cases (fresh vinegar versus used vinegar)
steps.terutzMaskana: Only fresh vinegar, whose sharpness is still intact, has the effect. Used vinegar does not.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: no roasting the פסח on a grill
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that one may not roast the פסח on a grill.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One may not roast the פסח...' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the opening words of the משנה. This sets up a question about that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that the פסח may not be roasted on a grill, because the hot metal would do the roasting instead of the fire. The same משנה then tells a story about רבן גמליאל roasting the פסח on a grill. That combination is what the גמרא is about to question.

phrases.english: One may not roast the Paschal lamb, etc.
phrases.notes: Quotes the משנה. The full line says 'on a grill'.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסח may not be roasted on a grill.

steps.title: Why does the story contradict the rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה tells a story that seems to contradict its own rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: A story that contradicts [the rule]?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem in the משנה. It forbids grilling the פסח, then tells a story where רבן גמליאל did exactly that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a story in a משנה is brought to support the rule. Here it seems to go against the rule, which makes no sense. So something in the משנה must be explained.

phrases.english: An incident to contradict [the rule]?!
phrases.notes: A classic question: a story should support the rule, not go against it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the משנה just quoted is put together.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way the משנה is organized: its rule and its story
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule forbids a grill, while the story describes using a grill. A story should not contradict the rule it comes with.

steps.title: A missing line: a grill with holes is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה has a missing line: a grill with holes is permitted, and the story was about that kind of grill.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is missing something, and this is what it means: if the grill has holes, it is permitted. And about this, רבי צדוק said: there was a story with רבן גמליאל, who told his slave טבי, 'Go and roast the פסח for us on the grill with holes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by filling in a line that is missing from the משנה. Once that line is added, the story supports the rule instead of contradicting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A solid grill is forbidden because the hot metal roasts the meat, not the fire. A grill with holes lets the fire reach the meat directly, so it is allowed. רבן גמליאל's story was about a grill with holes, so it fits the added line.

keyTerms.meaning: 'it is missing something', meaning the text has a gap
טבי, the slave of רבן גמליאל

steps.whatToRemember: A solid grill is forbidden for the פסח. A grill with holes is allowed, because the fire itself reaches the meat.
steps.confusionAlert: 'חסורי מיחסרא' does not mean the משנה is mistaken. It means the משנה is written briefly and a line has to be filled in.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea behind this answer, that the פסח must be roasted by the fire itself, is exactly what the rest of this passage is about.

phrases.english: It is incomplete, and this is what it teaches:
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's usual way of saying a line is missing, and it's about to fill it in.

phrases.english: And if it is a grill with holes, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: This is the missing line the גמרא is filling in.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Tzadok said:
There was an incident with Rabban Gamliel
who said to Tavi his slave:
Go and roast the Paschal lamb for us
on the perforated grill.
phrases.notes: Now the story matches the added line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in a missing line in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story seemed to allow any grill, which would contradict the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: A solid grill is forbidden, but a grill with holes is allowed. The story was about a grill with holes.

steps.title: Bread baked in a swept oven that was heated with ערלה peels
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר אידי asks: if an oven was heated with ערלה peels and then swept clean, is bread baked in it forbidden according to the strict view?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בר אידי asked רב אדא בר אהבה: An oven was heated with peels of ערלה, then swept out, and then bread was baked in it. According to the view that forbids such bread, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. It asks whether heat left in an oven after the forbidden fuel has been removed still counts as coming from that fuel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a view that bread baked over fire from ערלה fuel is forbidden, because the person gets benefit from the forbidden fuel. The question is whether that still applies once the fuel and ashes are swept out and only the leftover heat in the oven bakes the bread. In other words: is the oven's leftover heat the same as the fire itself?

keyTerms.meaning: he heated it, he lit it
peels of fruit from a tree's first three years, which may not be used for any benefit
he swept it out (removed the coals and ashes)
according to the one who forbids

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר אִידִי
phrases.english: Rav Ḥinnana bar Idi asked
of Rav Adda bar Ahava:
An oven that one heated with peels of orla
phrases.notes: The fuel is forbidden for any benefit.

phrases.english: and he swept it and baked bread in it,
phrases.notes: The fuel is gone; only the leftover heat remains.

phrases.english: according to the one who forbids, what is [the law]?
phrases.notes: Even the strict view, which forbids bread baked over ערלה fire, may allow it here.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר אִידִי מֵרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the theme of the פסח needing actual fire, and asks a related question about leftover oven heat.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the leftover heat in a swept oven still counts as benefit from the forbidden ערלה fuel.

steps.title: The bread is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה answers that the bread is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The bread is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא gives a short answer: once the oven has been swept, the bread is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the forbidden fuel was removed before baking, the bread was not baked by the ערלה fire. The leftover heat is not treated as benefit from the forbidden fuel.

phrases.english: He said to him: The bread is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bread baked in a swept oven that had been heated with ערלה peels is permitted, even according to the strict view.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוחנן: a swept oven is not 'roasted in fire'
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא challenges the answer using רבי יוחנן's teaching that a פסח roasted in a swept oven is not 'צלי אש', learned from the Torah saying 'צלי אש' twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But רב חיננא סבא said, in the name of רבי אסי, in the name of רבי יוחנן: If one heated an oven, swept it out, and roasted the פסח in it, that is not 'roasted in fire'. This is because the Torah says 'roasted in fire... roasted in fire', two times.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חיננא pushes back against רב אדא's answer by quoting רבי יוחנן. The answer to this challenge comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן needed the Torah to repeat 'צלי אש' twice to rule out a swept oven for the פסח. That suggests that without the extra words, the leftover heat would have counted as fire. If so, the leftover heat should also count as coming from the ערלה fuel, and the bread should be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'but didn't [so-and-so] say?', a phrase that opens a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן's teaching is about the מצוה of roasting the פסח, while the question was about the איסור of ערלה. The challenge works by comparing how the two cases treat leftover oven heat.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the discussion depends on whether the leftover heat in an oven counts as 'the fire' for every halacha, or only in some cases.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָאָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא סָבָא
phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't Rav Ḥinnana the Elder say
phrases.notes: Opens the challenge.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
phrases.notes: The chain of people who passed on the teaching.

phrases.english: An oven that one heated and swept
and roasted the Paschal lamb in it:
this is not 'roasted in fire',
as it is stated: 'roasted in fire... roasted in fire',
two times.
phrases.notes: The repeated words teach that it must be real fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָאָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא סָבָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא's ruling that bread baked in a swept oven heated with ערלה peels is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah had to repeat 'צלי אש' to rule out a swept oven for the פסח. That implies the leftover heat would otherwise count as fire, so for ערלה it should still count as benefit from the forbidden fuel.

steps.title: The inference that turns the swept-oven verse into a challenge
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא draws the conclusion from רבי יוחנן's teaching. A special verse was needed to exclude a swept oven, so without that verse a swept oven would count as fire. That means the bread in the ערלה case should be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only reason a swept oven is not 'roasted in fire' is that the תורה wrote 'צלי אש' twice. Without that, I would have said it does count as roasted in fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חיננא finishes his challenge. He shows that, by default, heat left in a swept oven counts as the fire's own heat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה had to add a verse to exclude a swept oven, then by normal logic that oven still counts as 'fire.' ערלה has no such special verse. So bread baked in a swept oven should still count as baked by the ערלה fire, which goes against רב אדא's ruling that it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (the תורה) revealed or made clear
Roasted in fire, the required way to cook the קרבן פסח
I would have thought (the default assumption before the verse)

steps.confusionAlert: This line does not rule that a swept oven counts as fire. It argues that it would have counted as fire if the extra verse were not written, and uses that to attack the lenient ruling about ערלה.

phrases.english: The reason is because the Merciful One revealed
"roasted in fire," "roasted in fire," two times.
But if the Merciful One had not revealed it,
I would have said it is roasted in fire.
phrases.notes: So the default is that a swept oven's heat counts as fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from Step 7 by drawing the inference from רבי יוחנן's teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's ruling (Step 6) that bread from a swept oven heated with ערלה is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse was needed to exclude a swept oven by פסח, so by default a swept oven counts as fire. ערלה has no such verse, so the bread should be forbidden.

steps.title: The rule was taught by פסח and applies everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא answers that the verse by פסח teaches a general rule: a swept oven is not 'fire.' We apply that rule to other areas, including ערלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: the תורה revealed it there, and we learn from it for other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא defends his ruling. The verse by פסח is not a special exception. It teaches a rule we use everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חיננא treated the verse as limited to פסח. רב אדא says the verse defines what 'fire' means in general. So in ערלה too, a swept oven does not count as the forbidden fire, and the bread is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in the case of the פסח)
We learn from it (we apply it to other cases)

phrases.english: He said to him: The Merciful One revealed it there,
and we learn from it.
phrases.notes: We apply the פסח rule to ערלה as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גַּלִּי רַחֲמָנָא הָתָם, וְיָלְפִינַן מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Broadening the verse: it is a general rule, not one limited to פסח.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse is a special rule only for פסח, so elsewhere a swept oven counts as fire.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse defines 'fire' for all areas, so the ערלה bread is permitted.

steps.title: A second answer: פסח depends on fire, but ערלה depends on the forbidden wood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another answer. By פסח the תורה cares about fire, so leftover heat might have seemed like fire, and a verse was needed. By ערלה the תורה cares about the forbidden wood, and once the oven is swept that wood is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: there, the verse was needed. Without it, I would have thought the תורה cares about fire, and even a swept oven is still 'roasted in fire.' But here the תורה cares about the forbidden wood, and it is no longer there.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second, different answer to the same challenge. It shows that the two cases are not alike in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question in each case is different. For פסח the issue is 'Was it cooked by fire?', and leftover heat could be called fire, so a verse had to exclude it. For ערלה the issue is benefiting from forbidden wood, and once the coals are swept out there is no forbidden wood left. So the bread is permitted even without any verse.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another answer)
He swept it out (removed the coals)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why bread from a swept oven heated with ערלה is permitted. (1) The פסח verse teaches a general rule that a swept oven is not 'fire.' (2) ערלה is about the forbidden wood, and swept-out wood is gone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a key idea: to decide whether something is forbidden, first ask what the prohibition actually depends on. Is it the fire itself, or the forbidden material?

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
There, the reason is that the Merciful One wrote
"roasted in fire" two times,
but had the Merciful One not written
"roasted in fire" two times,
I would have said: the Merciful One is particular about fire,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ גְּרָפוֹ נָמֵי — צְלִי אֵשׁ הוּא.
phrases.english: and even if he swept it out, it is still roasted in fire.
But here (by ערלה),
the Merciful One is particular about the forbidden wood,
and it is not here.
phrases.notes: The coals were swept out, so no forbidden wood remains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge of Step 8, as an alternative to Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the two prohibitions depend on different things.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פסח and ערלה work the same way, so if a swept oven counts as fire by default, the bread is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: פסח depends on fire, so a verse was needed. ערלה depends on the forbidden wood, which is gone, so the bread is permitted with no verse needed.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי says a פסח placed on coals counts as roasted in fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא. If someone cut up the פסח and placed it directly on coals, רבי rules that this is צלי אש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: if he cut it and placed it on coals, רבי says: I say this counts as roasted in fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new related topic. A ברייתא gives רבי's ruling that roasting on coals counts as fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling treats glowing coals as 'fire' for the מצוה of צלי אש. That is the premise the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: He cut it (made cuts in the meat)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he cut it and placed it on top of coals,
Rabbi says:
I say that this is roasted in fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חֲתָכוֹ, וּנְתָנוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי גֶּחָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new related topic about what counts as צלי אש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, a פסח roasted directly on coals is צלי אש.

steps.title: Does רבי really hold that coals are fire?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי raises a contradiction to רב חסדא. Did רבי really say that coals count as fire? This implies that another source, a ברייתא, says otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי raised a contradiction to רב חסדא: Did רבי really say that coals are fire?
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up a contradiction between רבי's ruling and another source. That source, a ברייתא that seems to treat coals as not fire, comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling in Step 11 treats coals as fire. The word רמי signals that another source (an anonymous ברייתא) seems to imply the opposite. So the challenge is whether רבי's ruling can stand against it.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction to him (sets two sources against each other)

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Achadvoi bar Ami raised a contradiction to Rav Chisda:
Did Rabbi say
that coals are fire?
phrases.notes: The contradicting source follows in the next part of the גמרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב אַחָדְבוּי בַּר אַמֵּי לְרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the premise of the ברייתא in Step 11 by setting it against another source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling that coals count as fire (Step 11).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another teaching of רבי (brought next) seems to treat coals as not fire. So רבי appears to contradict himself.

steps.title: The source of the contradiction: a burn from fire
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the doubled word 'מכוה מכוה' that a burn from a coal, hot ash, boiling lime, or fire-heated water counts as a 'burn from fire' for צרעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a contradiction. The ברייתא says: 'A burn from fire.' From this I only know a burn from fire itself. If someone was burned by a coal, hot ash, boiling lime, boiling plaster, or anything that gets its heat from fire, including fire-heated water, how do we know? The verse says 'a burn' twice, and this includes them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that רב אחדבוי בר אמי uses against רבי. This step brings the source. The next step draws the actual inference from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For צרעת, the תורה has special rules for skin that was 'burned by fire' (מכות אש). The ברייתא says plain 'fire' covers only real fire. It needs the doubled word מכוה to include a coal and the other hot things. Look closely: a coal is listed among the things that need the extra word.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction (two sources that seem to clash)
A burn from fire. This is a category in the laws of צרעת.
It included (the extra word adds more cases)

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
phrases.notes: Introduces a source that seems to clash with רבי's view.

phrases.english: "A burn from fire"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:24, in the laws of צרעת

phrases.english: I only know a case where it was burned by fire itself;
if it was burned by a coal, or by hot ash,
by boiling lime, or by boiling plaster,
or anything whose heat comes from the fire,
including water heated by fire, from where do we know?
The verse says "a burn," "a burn" twice, and this includes them.
phrases.notes: The doubled word adds the extra cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the contradiction announced in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling (step 11) that putting the פסח on coals counts as צלי אש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא needs an extra word to treat a coal-burn as a 'fire' burn. So the plain word 'fire' does not include coals.

steps.title: The inference: without the extra word, coals would not be fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the inference: only because of the doubled word do coals count, so without it coals are not 'fire.' This contradicts רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The only reason is that the תורה included them with 'a burn, a burn.' If the תורה had not included them that way, coals would not count as fire!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the contradiction. The ברייתא shows that plain 'fire' does not cover coals, but רבי said coals do count as fire for the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If coals were obviously fire, no extra word would be needed. The extra word shows that, by default, coals are not 'fire.' For the פסח, the תורה only says 'צלי אש' with no extra word. So coals should not be enough there, which goes against רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
That He included (from רִבָּה, to include). This is not the name רבי.

steps.confusionAlert: The word דְּרַבִּי here is NOT 'of רבי' (רבי יהודה הנשיא). It means 'that He included.' Read it as: 'The reason is that the Merciful One included.'

phrases.english: The reason is that the Merciful One included them with
phrases.notes: דְּרַבִּי means 'that He included,' not the name רבי.

phrases.english: "a burn," "a burn";
but if the Merciful One had not included them with
"a burn," "a burn,"
then coals would not be fire!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי רַחֲמָנָא ״מִכְוָה״ ״מִכְוָה״, הָא לָא רַבִּי רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenging inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's view that coals count as fire (צלי אש)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word was needed to include coals. So by default 'fire' does not include coals, and roasting on coals for the פסח should not be צלי אש.

steps.title: A wood coal is obviously fire; the verse is needed for hot metal
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a burning wood coal is plainly fire and needs no verse. The doubled word is needed only for a red-hot piece of metal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A wood coal does not need a verse to include it. A verse is needed only for a hot piece of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא, defending רבי, explains that the ברייתא's extra word is not about wood coals at all. It is about hot metal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A glowing wood coal is still burning, so it is real fire, and רבי's ruling stands. The 'coal' the ברייתא needed to include is a piece of metal heated in a fire. Metal has no flame of its own, so we might have thought it is not 'fire.' This removes the contradiction.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A coal of wood
does not need a verse to include it.
Where a verse is needed
is for a red-hot piece of metal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גַּחֶלֶת שֶׁל עֵץ לָא אִיצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא לְרַבּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 14 by narrowing what the ברייתא's 'coal' refers to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא's extra word refers to metal, not wood coals.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא needed a verse for wood coals, so coals are not fire, which goes against רבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wood coals are plainly fire, so רבי is right. The verse is only needed to include hot metal.

steps.title: Challenge from בת כהן: hot metal is called fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. For a בת כהן, the תורה says 'she shall be burned in fire,' and רב מתנה says this was done with molten lead. So hot metal is plainly 'fire.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And are hot pieces of metal not fire? But by a בת כהן it is written, 'In fire she shall be burned,' and רב מתנה said: They would make for her a bar of lead!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer just given. It brings proof that the תורה already calls hot metal 'fire,' so no extra verse should be needed to include it. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The penalty of שריפה for a בת כהן was carried out by pouring molten lead into her mouth. Yet the תורה calls this 'באש,' with fire. So the plain word 'fire' already covers hot metal. Then the extra word in the ברייתא cannot be for metal, and the contradiction to רבי returns.

keyTerms.meaning: A daughter of a כהן who sinned with adultery. Her punishment is שְׂרֵפָה.
In fire she shall be burned (ויקרא 21:9)
A bar of lead, melted and poured into the mouth

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא tests an answer: it checks whether the new definition (hot metal is not plain 'fire') fits other places in the תורה.

phrases.aramaic: וְגֶחָלִים שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת לָאו אֵשׁ הוּא?
phrases.english: And are hot pieces of metal not fire?
But regarding the daughter of a priest,
it is written: "In fire she shall be burned."
And Rav Mattana said:

phrases.aramaic: פְּתִילָה שֶׁל אֲבָר הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין לָהּ!
phrases.english: They would prepare a bar of lead for her!
phrases.notes: Molten lead was poured down her throat. The תורה calls this 'fire.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגֶחָלִים שֶׁל מַתֶּכֶת לָאו אֵשׁ הוּא? וְהָא גַּבֵּי בַּת כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 15 that hot metal needs a special verse to count as fire.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 15 that the ברייתא's extra word is needed for hot metal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה calls execution by molten lead 'באש,' so hot metal is plainly fire. Then no extra word is needed for metal, and the ברייתא's extra word must be for wood coals after all.

steps.title: The extra word 'she shall be burned' includes every kind of burning
steps.stepSummary: With a בת כהן, hot metal counts as fire only because the extra word 'תשרף' includes all burnings that come from fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the verse says 'in fire she shall be burned.' The word 'she shall be burned' comes to include all burnings that come from fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 16. With a בת כהן, molten lead counts as 'fire' only because the verse has an extra word that includes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 tried to prove that hot metal is plainly fire, since the בת כהן is executed with molten lead. The answer is that molten lead counts there only because of the extra word 'תשרף'. So hot metal is not plainly fire after all, and it is fine that צרעת also needs its doubled word 'מכוה מכוה' to include it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there; that case is not comparable
In fire she shall be burned (the verse about a בת כהן)
To include; an extra word that widens the law
Burnings that come from fire, such as hot metal

steps.whyThisMatters: It saves the תירוץ of step 15: a wood coal is plainly fire, but hot metal needs a verse, both for צרעת and for a בת כהן.

phrases.english: It is different there, as the verse says:
"In fire she shall be burned"
"She shall be burned" comes to include
phrases.notes: The extra word is the source that includes other burnings.

phrases.english: all burnings that come from fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by showing that molten lead for a בת כהן comes from an extra word.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: that law rests on a special verse that includes hot metal
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בת כהן case proves that hot metal is plainly 'fire'.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hot metal counts as fire there only because 'תשרף' includes it, so it is not plainly fire.

steps.title: Then why not burn her with real fire from branches?
steps.stepSummary: If every burning from fire counts, real fire surely counts. So why not surround her with bundles of branches?
steps.simpleTranslation: And all the more so fire itself counts. So let us surround her with bundles of branches and burn her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the method of execution. If even indirect burnings count, real fire counts all the more, so why use molten lead at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the verse includes all burnings that come from fire. That makes ordinary fire the most obvious way to fulfill 'in fire she shall be burned.' So why do we need molten lead instead of simply burning her with branches?

keyTerms.meaning: Bundles of vine branches used as firewood

phrases.english: And all the more so fire itself.
So let us surround her with bundles of branches
and burn her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the inclusion in step 17 to question why molten lead is used.
steps.kashyaTarget: The method of executing a בת כהן with molten lead (רב מתנה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If all burnings from fire count, real fire counts even more, so molten lead seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The burning must be like the sons of Aaron: the soul burns, the body stays whole
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה from the death of the sons of אהרן teaches that this שריפה burns the soul while the body remains intact.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from the word 'burning' here and the word 'burning' by בני אהרן. Just as there it was a burning of the soul while the body remained, so too here it is a burning of the soul while the body remains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the execution must copy the way the sons of אהרן died. That rules out a bonfire of branches, which destroys the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שריפה' appears both by the בת כהן and by the sons of אהרן. Fire went into the sons of אהרן and burned them inside, while their bodies stayed whole. The גזירה שוה applies that model here: burn inside and keep the body intact, which molten lead poured down the throat does.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison between two verses that share the same word
The sons of אהרן, נדב and אביהוא, who were burned by fire from Heaven
Burning of the soul while the body remains whole

phrases.english: It is learned from "burning" and "burning"
phrases.notes: The same word in two places creates a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: from the sons of Aaron.
Just as there, it was a burning of the soul
while the body remained,
so too here, it is a burning of the soul
while the body remains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by showing that the required kind of burning rules out ordinary fire.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A גזירה שוה that defines what kind of burning is required
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any fire would do, so a bonfire of branches is fine.
steps.terutzMaskana: The burning must destroy the soul and leave the body whole, like the sons of אהרן, so molten lead is used.

steps.title: Then why not use boiling water heated by fire?
steps.stepSummary: Boiling water also burns inside without destroying the body. So why not use it instead of molten lead?
steps.simpleTranslation: So let us execute her with water heated by fire?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. Boiling water also counts as a burning that comes from fire and would leave the body whole, so why not use it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 included all burnings that come from fire, and fire-heated water is one of them (like the water in step 13). Boiling water would also burn inside while keeping the body intact. So the גזירה שוה alone does not explain why molten lead in particular is chosen.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us do it to her (carry out the execution this way)

phrases.english: So let us execute her with water heated by fire?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 19 but asks why molten lead is chosen over another method that fits it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of molten lead specifically
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Boiling water satisfies both the inclusion (a burning from fire) and the גזירה שוה (body stays whole).

steps.title: Choose a kind death: love your fellow as yourself
steps.stepSummary: Because of רב נחמן's rule, learned from 'love your fellow as yourself', the court must choose the quickest and kindest death. Molten lead is quicker than boiling water.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of רב נחמן, for רב נחמן said: The verse says 'And you shall love your fellow as yourself.' Choose for him a nice death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that boiling water would be a slow, painful death. The rule is that even when executing, the court picks the kindest way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן learns from 'love your fellow as yourself' that a condemned person deserves the easiest possible death. Molten lead kills almost at once, while boiling water would drag out the suffering. So molten lead is required.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall love your fellow as yourself
Choose for him a nice (kind, quick) death

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule of מיתה יפה shapes how the court carries out all of its executions.

phrases.english: It is because of the teaching of רב נחמן,
for רב נחמן said: The verse says:
"And you shall love your fellow as yourself"
Choose for him a nice death.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב נַחְמָן, דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by adding a principle that rules out boiling water.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Boiling water is just as good as molten lead.
steps.terutzMaskana: Molten lead is used because it gives a quicker, kinder death.

steps.title: If we have רב נחמן, why do we need the גזירה שוה?
steps.stepSummary: Since רב נחמן's principle already pushes us to the kindest death, the גזירה שוה from the sons of אהרן seems unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since we have רב נחמן's rule, why do I need the גזירה שוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether the earlier source is needed. Perhaps רב נחמן's principle alone would already lead us to molten lead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Molten lead is the kindest death, and רב נחמן requires the kindest death. If that alone brings us to molten lead, then the גזירה שוה of step 19 seems to add nothing. The גמרא asks what it is really teaching.

phrases.english: But since we have רב נחמן's rule,
why do I need the גזירה שוה?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּאִיכָּא רַב נַחְמָן, גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at both sources (steps 19 and 21) and asks whether one makes the other unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the גזירה שוה from the sons of אהרן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן's principle alone seems to lead to molten lead, so the גזירה שוה looks extra.

steps.title: Each source teaches something the other cannot
steps.stepSummary: Without the גזירה שוה, we would think burning the soul with the body intact is not 'burning' at all. With only רב נחמן, we would simply use a huge fire so she dies fast. The גזירה שוה teaches that molten lead counts as שריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Without the גזירה שוה, I would have said that burning the soul while the body remains is not 'burning' at all. And if we had only רב נחמן's rule, we would add many bundles of branches so that she dies quickly. So the גזירה שוה teaches us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why both sources are needed. רב נחמן's principle alone would lead to a big, fast bonfire, not molten lead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse demands 'שריפה'. Without the גזירה שוה, burning only inside might not count as שריפה. Then רב נחמן's principle would just mean making the fire bigger so she dies faster. The גזירה שוה shows that inner burning is a real שריפה, and only then does רב נחמן's principle choose molten lead over boiling water.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (an initial mistaken assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three layers. The extra word 'תשרף' includes all burnings from fire. The גזירה שוה from the sons of אהרן requires burning the soul with the body intact. רב נחמן's 'מיתה יפה' picks the kindest such method. Together they lead to molten lead.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן alone does not lead to molten lead. Without the גזירה שוה, kindness would only mean a bigger, faster fire, because burning inside would not yet count as שריפה.

phrases.english: They say: If not for the גזירה שוה,
I would have said:
burning the soul while the body remains
is not 'burning' at all.
And if it were only because of רב נחמן's rule,
we would add many bundles of branches for her,
so that she would die quickly.
So the גזירה שוה teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: אִי לָאו גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22 by showing that the גזירה שוה and רב נחמן each do a separate job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that each source is needed (צריכותא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's principle alone would lead to molten lead, so the גזירה שוה is unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without the גזירה שוה, inner burning would not count as שריפה and we would use a bigger fire. The גזירה שוה makes molten lead a valid שריפה, and רב נחמן chooses it as the kindest method.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק need the word 'in fire'?
steps.stepSummary: If 'תשרף' already includes every kind of burning, what does the word 'באש' add?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need the word 'in fire'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own reading. If 'she shall be burned' covers every kind of burning, the word 'באש' seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous steps established that molten lead counts as שריפה. If 'תשרף' is that broad, then 'באש' looks like it adds nothing. The גמרא assumes no word in the תורה is wasted, so it must teach something.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (a question about an extra word)

phrases.english: But then, why do I need 'in fire'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the broad reading of 'תשרף' that made molten lead acceptable.
steps.kashyaTarget: The broad reading of 'תשרף' as including all burning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'תשרף' includes everything, the word 'באש' would be wasted.

steps.title: 'In fire' excludes lead that was never heated by fire
steps.stepSummary: 'באש' teaches that the burning must come from fire. This excludes lead that is hot in its natural state.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude lead from its source, meaning lead that was not heated by fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'באש' excludes lead that is hot in its natural state from its source, without being heated by fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תשרף' widens the law to every burning that comes from fire. 'באש' sets the limit: the heat must actually come from fire. So both words are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: From its source, in its original state

steps.whatToRemember: 'תשרף' includes every burning that comes from fire. 'באש' requires that the heat really come from fire.

phrases.english: To exclude lead from its source.
phrases.notes: Lead that is hot naturally, not heated by fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the extra word 'באש'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word its own job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'באש' seemed extra once 'תשרף' was read broadly.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'באש' excludes heat that does not come from fire, such as lead hot from its source.

steps.title: The פרים הנשרפים must be burned only in real fire
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא: for the פרים הנשרפים, 'באש' limits the burning to real fire, so why is בת כהן different?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: Wherever it says 'in fire shall it be burned', does it come to include every burning that comes from fire? But for the bulls that are burned it says 'and he shall burn it on wood in fire', and a ברייתא teaches: 'In fire', and not in burning lime or burning plaster!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה challenges the broad reading. For the פרים הנשרפים, the same idea of 'fire' and 'burning' is read narrowly, and only real fire is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בת כהן, 'burning' includes things like molten lead. For the פרים, a ברייתא says burning lime or plaster is not allowed, only real fire. Similar words seem to be read in opposite ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Bulls whose bodies are burned outside the camp

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
And wherever it is written 'in fire shall it be burned',

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל שְׂרֵיפוֹת הַבָּאוֹת מֵחֲמַת אֵשׁ הוּא?
phrases.english: does it come to include all burnings that come from fire?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא גַּבֵּי פָּרִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִים, דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ:
phrases.english: But regarding the bulls that are burned, about which it is written:
'And he shall burn it on wood in fire',
phrases.notes: ויקרא ד:יב

phrases.english: and it was taught: 'In fire', and not in burning lime,
and not in burning plaster?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא וְכֹל הֵיכָא דִּכְתִיב בָּאֵשׁ תִּשָּׂרֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the broad reading of 'burning' by comparing it to another פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that 'fire' plus 'burning' includes every burning that comes from fire
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא reads the פרים verse narrowly, allowing only real fire, which contradicts the broad reading for בת כהן.

steps.title: The word order makes the difference
steps.stepSummary: For בת כהן, 'fire' comes first and 'burned' comes last, which widens the law. For the פרים, 'fire' comes last, which limits it to fire only.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How can you compare them? There it says 'in fire' and then 'she shall be burned', which includes all burnings that come from fire. Here it says 'and he shall burn it on wood in fire', with 'fire' at the end, to tell you: fire, yes; anything else, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא rejects the comparison. He says the order of the words in each פסוק changes the meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When 'burning' is the last word, the פסוק ends on the general idea of burning, so it includes any burning caused by fire. When 'fire' is the last word, the פסוק ends on fire itself, so only real fire is allowed. That is why lime and plaster are excluded for the פרים.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (rejects a comparison)

steps.confusionAlert: Both פסוקים use 'fire' and 'burning'. The difference is only which word comes last, and the last word decides how wide the law is.

phrases.english: He said to him: How can you compare?!
There it is written 'in fire' and afterward 'she shall be burned' —
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the בת כהן.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבּוֹת כׇּל שְׂרֵיפוֹת הַבָּאוֹת מֵחֲמַת הָאֵשׁ.
phrases.english: to include all burnings that come from fire.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא כְּתִיב ״וְשָׂרַף אֹתוֹ עַל עֵצִים בָּאֵשׁ״
phrases.english: Here it is written 'and he shall burn it on wood in fire'
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the פרים הנשרפים.

phrases.english: with 'fire' at the end,
to say that fire — yes,
anything else — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה by separating the two פסוקים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by word order
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seemed to say the same thing and should be read the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ending with 'burned' widens the law. Ending with 'fire' limits it to real fire.

steps.title: The פרים verse also ends with burning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: in the passage about the פרים, burning also appears at the end. It is about to quote that פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, burning is written at the end, as it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's word-order answer. It says the פרים passage also ends with a word of burning, and it sets up a quote that continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's distinction depended on the פרים verse ending with 'fire'. If that same passage also ends with 'burned', the distinction falls apart and the original question returns.

phrases.english: There too, burning is written at the end,
phrases.notes: 'There' is talking about the פרים הנשרפים.

phrases.english: as it is written:
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the word-order distinction just given.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that the פרים verse ends with 'fire'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same פסוק also ends with burning, so by רבי זירא's own rule it should include all burnings.
